You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

For ARC inputs made of large uniform rectangular tiles separated by a one-cell lattice of a different base/separator color, with sparse marker colors at lattice intersections, read the intersection colors as a vertex matrix. For every adjacent 2x2 vertex group, output its shared color only when all four corners match; otherwise use the tile/interior background color. Ignore the separator color as a marker. Then crop the result to the smallest bounding rectangle containing all shared-color cells; retain background-valued gaps inside that box, and omit all-background margins outside. Example: a 27x19 demo with background 8, marker 1 in cell (0,0), and marker 3 in (2,1) produced [[1,8],[8,8],[8,3]], cropping away one all-background top row. Confirmed on task-f63064b0: a lattice with 3x4 interior tiles of 7, matching-corner cells were 4 at (0,0), 2 at (0,2), 8 at (2,0), 1 at (2,2) and (3,2); cropped output [[4,7,2],[7,7,7],[8,7,1],[7,7,1]] was correct. Earlier evidence: a 5x5 vertex lattice with interior 9 and markers 7/8 produced 4x4 output where only cells with four matching corners retained the marker; a 4x4 vertex lattice on separator 2 / interior 0 produced [[0,7,7],[0,0,0],[7,0,8]].

Additional confirmation (task-f63064b0, 2026-10-21): On a 21x28 grid with interior/background 1, separator lattice color 7, horizontal lattice rows 5 and 16, and vertical lattice columns 1, 13, and 25, all six intersections were marker 5. The output was [[5,5]]: one output cell per adjacent pair of horizontal/vertical lattice coordinates, with each cell taking the shared color iff all four corner markers agree; crop away all-background output margins. This also confirms rectangular, non-square lattice spacing is fine.
